closure_matrix_v0_6.original_title: The registered S2/S3 single-position restricted-logit rule is not implementable under any pinned role tokenizer, because each complete candidate surface is two tokens
closure_matrix_v0_6.repair: The visible answer surface is preserved exactly. The answer cue remains 'Answer:' with no trailing whitespace, and each complete candidate surface remains one U+0020 followed by one registered digit. What changes is where the decision statistic is read. Every complete S2/S3 candidate factors as candidate_d = common_prefix || discriminant_d. The scoring context is the registered prompt token IDs followed by the verified common-prefix token, formed by concatenation and never by re-encoding a concatenated string. One ordinary prefill evaluation is performed on that context and the next-token logit vector is read only at the ten verified discriminant token IDs. The deterministic restricted argmax is mapped back to the complete registered candidate surface. The common prefix is a teacher-forced candidate prefix: it is not a prompt-rendering change, not a generated token and not a separate sequence-level model evaluation. S3 reuses the exact S2 discriminant-position logit vector on CPU and adds zero model evaluations.
closure_matrix_v0_6.residual_limitation: The registration holds for the three currently pinned role tokenizers, and only for them. The equivalence is claimed for candidates of equal two-token length sharing one common prefix under a deterministic argmax; it is not extended to arbitrary multi-token candidates, unequal lengths, non-common prefixes, summed log probabilities, free generation or any tokenizer that is not separately pinned and verified.
closure_matrix_v0_6.verification: the common-prefix token and the ten discriminant token IDs are DERIVED from the immutable published P0-T result and the frozen corpus by studies/study3/pilot/p0_r1/p0_r1_factorization.py, which performs zero tokenizer encodes and imports no tokenizer library. The derivation recovers the byte string each token contributes by solving, over 70 published (prompt, token-ID) pairs per role, for a segmentation consistent with every sequence; the common-prefix token and each discriminant token are required to be UNIQUELY determined by that evidence. The result is common prefix 220 carrying exactly one U+0020 and discriminants 15 through 24 carrying '0' through '9', identically for RT, RL and RI. A committed test asserts that no member of {220, 15..24} appears as a numeric literal anywhere in the verifier, so the identities cannot have been transcribed.

closure_matrix_v0_6.original_title: The P0-T eligibility classifier consulted a role-level flag and propagated a role-level S2 failure onto 27 mechanically valid S1 cells, producing ineligible rows with empty reason lists and an over-severe terminal state
closure_matrix_v0_6.repair: A versioned successor classifier computes eligibility at the narrowest applicable key: candidate-surface eligibility at role x profile, presentation-pair distinctness at role x profile x contrast, structural absence at profile x contrast, and target-role executability at role. Every reason carries its own scope, and the production validator rejects any reason whose scope is not a prefix of the cell it is attached to, so a failure cannot cross a profile, a role or a contrast. An ineligible row with an empty reason list is a validator failure rather than an output. S4 is diagnostic-only and can never satisfy target-role executability. not_applicable is structural absence and is never instantiated, never eligible, never ineligible, never a pass, never a zero, never a denominator row and never robustness evidence. The historical P0-T result is not edited: the correction is computed in a new derived view.
closure_matrix_v0_6.residual_limitation: The corrected matrix is a derived view over immutable historical observations. It does not re-run the census, does not create new encodes and does not rewrite the emitted historical terminal state, which remains attached to the consumed P0-T result as historical text.
